source.description: deploy sudoers grant with NOPASSWD systemctl

sink.description: deploy user can run systemctl as root without password

flow.description: sudoers policy grants the deploy user root systemctl capability

finding.description: The sudoers change lets the deploy user run /usr/bin/systemctl as root with NOPASSWD and no unit/action allowlist, so the deploy principal now has broad root service-control capability.
finding.suggested_fix: Constrain sudoers to an exact systemctl action and unit, or require a password/approval gate for privileged service operations.

results.evidence_notes: Line 3 grants deploy NOPASSWD root access to /usr/bin/systemctl. Sudoers command matching permits arguments unless explicitly constrained, so this is a concrete broad systemctl capability with no unit/action allowlist.

proof_by_construction.trigger: Apply the sudoers change, then the deploy user runs `sudo /usr/bin/systemctl restart sshd.service`.
preconditions: The deploy principal receives the reviewed sudoers policy.
